sermon.title: Many Adversaries Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this second part Pastor David G. Kincer explains that the Old Testament has civil laws, spiritual laws and shadow laws that point to Jesus, using the shadow of a cross. He ties this to communion, assembling, praise and baptism, explains why people were stoned, and says Jesus fulfilled the shadow laws and is the only way.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions read “Mr. Salvage”; this is corrected to “Savage” to match the name spoken in the same message (“Dan Savage”). The pastor names several public figures in this message; their names appear in the transcript only. He says the man stoned for gathering sticks was “in Exodus”; that account is in Numbers 15:32–36. The vineyard story he attributes to “Nabal” is told of Naboth in 1 Kings 21 (Nabal is a different person in 1 Samuel 25); his words are kept as captioned. “In Hebrews” (the sacrifice of praise) is Hebrews 13:15, and “Psalms 14” is Psalm 14. Several quoted verses are not named in the recording and are shown as quoted only. Four spots are marked [unclear] where the captions were garbled: a list of items after “holy water” (caption “Gri Maro”), the word before “night” in the virgin example (caption “wither”), the answer after “Who fulfilled the shadow laws?” (caption “G.”), and the last sentence about students (caption “of Paul audited”).

chunks.section_question: What are the three kinds of laws in the Old Testament?
chunks.short_answer: He says there are civil laws (like “Thou shalt not murder”), which carry a punishment; spiritual laws (like seek the Lord and pray); and shadow laws. He says critics are “confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.”
chunks.text: What people don’t understand is there’s three kinds of laws in the Bible in the Old Testament. Are you ready? There’s civil laws. All right? Thou shalt not murder. That’s a civil law and it has a punishment if you break it. Then there are spiritual laws. Seek the Lord your God and you will find him. Pray, you know, come before him and sing. See that’s spiritual laws. And then there is shadow laws. As we heard earlier, shadow laws. Say the word shadow. Yeah. And this is what these people are confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.

chunks.section_question: What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Hebrews 10:1, the law is a “shadow of good things to come,” and uses a shadow of a cross: from the shadow alone you cannot tell its color or material, but following it leads you to the real cross. In the same way, shadow laws “point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ.”
chunks.text:
Now don’t look at me like that. I’m telling you the truth. Hebrews 10:1: “For the law having a— what? Shadow of good things to come.” Say it. Shadow of good things to come. “And not the very image of the things can never with these sacrifices which they offer year by year make those who approach perfect.” But you see, they pointed to Jesus who can make you perfect. Now, you see up there on the screen a shadow of a cross. Now, because you’re an intelligent society, you know that’s a cross, isn’t it? But can you tell me the color of that cross?

Can you tell me the dimensions of that cross? Can you tell me if it’s made of metal, wood, plastic, stone? No, all you can tell me is what? It’s a cross. And if I follow the shadow, I will get to what? The real cross. And I’ll see its color. I’ll know its dimensions. I’ll know its purpose. And so, you can’t understand the details of God’s words by following shadow laws. They point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ. Amen. Now, folks, that’s good stuff. And this is what Mr. Savage and Mr. Bush and Mr. Obama and Oprah has got all mixed up.

He says “when you bash the Bible who points to Christ, you are bashing Christ” and removing the force that can change your life.

chunks.section_question: How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Lord’s table reminds us that Jesus died for our sins and gives new life, and we miss the point if we take communion but “don’t go to the real thing.” He says we assemble to be “stirred up to love one another” and do good when we leave, not for music or drama.
chunks.text:
See, they embraced the shadow. Is this clear to you? Now, watch this. Let’s bring it up to date. The Lord’s table. Jesus said, as of— do you do this in what? Remembrance of me. It reminds us that he died for our sins that we can get forgiveness even as a Christian. And he gives us that new life, that resurrection. That’s what the communion table’s for. But when we just take communion and embrace communion and don’t go to the real thing, we live any way we want, don’t we? Let’s take another one.

Assembling together. The Bible says, “Assembling yourself together, even the more so as you see the day approaching, stirring up one another to love and to good works.” See, that’s why we come together is to remind ourselves that we are to go out and be a light to this world that they may see our good works. That’s the purpose of assembling. It’s not music. It’s not drama. It’s not some prophet or priest. It’s we are supposed to be stirred up to love one another, not hurt one another, and do good when we leave. It’s not having a bell ringing message and you know some athlete come in and give their testimony or whatever. We should come to church too like the old the New Testament church when the Roman leaders wrote to each other about the church.

But what do most American Christians embrace? Do they embrace the shadow of the thing or do they really get the reality of the thing? See, we’re putting confidence in our church. We’re putting confidence in our baptism. We’re putting confidence and I take communion on Sunday when it should be pointing us to Jesus Christ and living for him. And that’s a good place for an amen. chunks.section_question: Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)
chunks.short_answer: He cites John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it,” and says it was impossible because they were constantly unclean and “spent all their life trying to get clean.” He says the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what it pointed to, and warns we are in danger of doing the same.
chunks.text: John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it.” Why didn’t they keep it? Because it was impossible. Them guys were unclean every day. If they had sex with their spouse, they were unclean. If a bug landed on their— a bug landed on their plate or whatever, they were unclean. Every time you turn around, they’re unclean. They’re unclean. They spent all their life trying to get clean. The the shadow laws were impossible to keep. And yet the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what the shadow pointed to. And today we are embracing the shadow and to what the shadow points to. We’re in danger of that. Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?
chunks.short_answer: He begins to address homosexuality by saying the food and clothing laws were “examples of living holy,” and that nobody was stoned in the Bible for the woman who lied about being a virgin: “Zero.” He says the one man stoned for working on Saturday was “an example of the judgment of God,” and that the real issue is an eternal price.
chunks.text:
Now, let me address homosexuality. Now, we we address the food, the clothing, the different clothing. It was all examples of living holy. Okay? The virgin or the woman that wasn’t a virgin on her [unclear] night, she got stoned because she said she was a virgin. They didn’t put that in there and she wasn’t. She lied and and she went into a marriage with a lie and deception. And you know how many people were stoned for that in the Bible? Zero. Interesting, isn’t it? Why? It’s a shadow law. God didn’t put it there for us to go around killing people that sinned.

faqs.question: Can you understand God’s word by following the shadow laws?
faqs.answer: He says no: “you can’t understand the details of God’s words by following shadow laws. They point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with these same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make those who approach perfect.

faqs.question: Did Jesus come to make us new people?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “old things passed away,” and Jesus “has the power to fulfill” God’s destiny for us.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

faqs.question: What does he say the shadow laws were for in Isaiah 1?
faqs.answer: He says after rejecting the empty sacrifices, God says, “Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean,” and “Cease to do evil and learn to do good.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes. Cease to do evil, Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor; Defend the fatherless, Plead for the widow.

faqs.question: Why does he say we assemble together?
faqs.answer: He says it is “to remind ourselves that we are to go out and be a light to this world that they may see our good works.” He says, “It’s not music. It’s not drama.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

faqs.question: What does he say the early church did every Sunday?
faqs.answer: He says Roman leaders wrote that Christians “get together on Sunday and they make a vow not to do wrong,” and “Every Sunday they kept repeating the vow.”

faqs.question: What does he say baptism means?
faqs.answer: He says a baptism certificate alone “doesn’t mean a hill of beans”; baptism reminds you that Jesus died for your sins and made you a new man. Whenever we see someone baptized, we are reminded that “we’re new creatures.”

faqs.question: What does he say about people who look for fault in the church?
faqs.answer: He says “You can’t be good enough for people that are trying to find something to criticize the church about.” He says, “You don’t want to mess around with God’s people.”

faqs.question: How many people does he say were stoned for picking up sticks on Saturday?
faqs.answer: He says one, “to give us an example of the judgment of God.” He says God is in “his saving timetable right now” but will judge when he comes again.

Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.” So, as the LORD commanded Moses, all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died.

faqs.question: What does he say about people who say they are perfect?
faqs.answer: He says if you say you’re “Mr. Perfect, you’re lying through your teeth,” and suggests asking somebody who works with you or lives with you in your home.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; A stranger, and not your own lips.

faqs.question: What does he say happens when a believer sins and confesses?
faqs.answer: He says “The shadow laws could not do, Jesus can do,” and that when we sin and confess, “He’s reliable. He’s faithful. He forgives. And we go on.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

faqs.question: What does he say Jesus said about the law and the prophets?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus came “not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfill them,” and that “Jesus plainly said he did.” He adds that “The law was our school master to bring us to Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Do not think that I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to destroy but to fulfill.
Therefore the law was our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

faqs.question: Why does he say we need these answers?
faqs.answer: He says, “We need to be able to answer them back,” and that we need to reach all people and “Bring them to Christ.”
